template_name: LZ Tools Developer Carousel Master Template
use_case: Instagram carousel 4:5, TOFU to soft marketing, developer-focused

brand.name: LZ Tools
brand.core_value_proposition: Convert website/web app to Android APK in under 5 minutes for suitable projects, directly through Telegram.
positioning: Do not position LZ Tools as a replacement for native Android development.
Position it as a faster path for Web-to-APK packaging when the web app is already ready.
Emphasize reduced setup, less repetitive configuration, and faster shipping.
taglines: Coding-nya sudah selesai. Jangan biarkan packaging-nya yang makan waktu.

background.notes: Avoid pure flat black when possible; use very subtle vignette or tonal depth.

body.style: clean sans-serif or monospace depending context

code.usage: terminal, JSON, build log, labels, small technical notes

content_strategy.funnel: TOFU → insight → soft solution reveal → CTA
rules: Start from a real developer pain point, not from product features.
Do not mention LZ Tools prominently before slide 4.
Use concrete Android build friction such as Gradle, SDK, dependency, manifest, keystore, permissions, testing, rebuild.
Avoid implying all Android development can be replaced by a web wrapper.
Prefer 'for suitable Web-to-APK use cases' framing.
Keep one dominant message per slide.
Use product proof or real Telegram UI on slide 4 or 5.

slide_framework.goal: Stop the scroll with a familiar Android developer situation.
slide_framework.content_formula: Completed dev work + unresolved APK packaging pain.
slide_framework.visual: Large headline + grey JSON/code card showing UI/backend/API/database done, APK build pending.

slide_framework.goal: Make the audience feel the toolchain friction.
slide_framework.content_formula: Small output, disproportionately long build/toolchain process.
slide_framework.visual: BUILD FAILED terminal with Gradle, SDK, dependency, manifest, signing, WebView/permission issues.

slide_framework.goal: Show that some Web-to-APK jobs are simple in intent but heavy in setup.
slide_framework.content_formula: Client asks for APK from ready web app; developer sees long setup checklist.
slide_framework.recommended_headline: CUMA MAU BIKIN APK DARI WEB.

slide_framework.goal: Introduce a real workflow and prove simplicity.
slide_framework.content_formula: Ready web + Telegram bot + selectable permissions/features + build.
slide_framework.recommended_headline: KALAU WEB-NYA SUDAH SIAP, KENAPA HARUS MULAI DARI NOL?
slide_framework.visual: Use real or realistic Telegram bot UI, ideally based on an actual LZ Tools flow.

slide_framework.goal: Show the result and invite trial.
slide_framework.content_formula: Web URL → bot → APK ready → download.
slide_framework.visual: Telegram bot on phone + APK READY result card + CTA button.

master_prompt.instruction: Create a 4:5 Instagram carousel slide for LZ Tools using the master visual system below. The slide must look like a premium dark developer interface rather than a conventional advertisement.
layout_rules: Keep the main headline in the upper third.
Keep the main UI/code card in the middle 45-55% of the canvas.
Use the bottom area for a short insight, CTA, or navigation arrow.
Slide counter must sit in the upper-right corner.
Do not let text touch the edges.

dynamic_fields.section_label: {{ANDROID DEVELOPER / LZ TOOLS / WEB TO APK}}
dynamic_fields.headline: {{HEADLINE}}

master_prompt.image_generation_prompt: Design a premium 4:5 developer carousel poster for LZ Tools. Use a near-black charcoal background, muted grey floating cards, thin blue-grey borders, crisp white and pale-blue typography, monospace technical details, and a minimalist terminal/code-editor aesthetic. Preserve generous negative space and mobile readability. Headline: '{{HEADLINE}}'. Supporting copy: '{{SUPPORTING_COPY}}'. Main content should visually represent '{{MAIN_UI_TYPE}}' with: '{{UI_CONTENT}}'. Add '{{SECTION_LABEL}}' in small monospace text at top-left and '{{SLIDE_NUMBER}} / 05' at top-right. Footer message: '{{FOOTER_MESSAGE}}'. CTA: '{{CTA_OR_EMPTY}}'. The design should feel made by developers for developers: technically credible, understated, premium, and not like a generic SaaS ad. Use only a few functional accent colors: pale blue for emphasis, green for success, red only for errors, yellow only for warnings. Do not use chibi, 3D characters, stock photography, bright gradients, excessive glow, or visual clutter.
